This is the single foundational operator; MMP (removal-only), LOX (formation+maturation-only) and realignment (turnover under a traction field) are all specializations of it. Replacing the lumped athermal axial spring with the real force-extension law is the mechanistic-over-lumped move mandated by the hard rule.

items.deliverable: LOX crosslink-formation + MMP severing kinetics on the fibrillar network; emergent <z>(c) and traction-induced stiffening reproducing the c^2 scaling as pure emergence; coupling to fa_ecm cell traction for a static/quasi-static remodeling demo, verified in an interactive HTML viewer.
items.blocker: Cell-coupled remodeling UNDER LOAD partially shares the native FF crawl DRAG blocker (Sigma-gamma ~ Nc, solver instability); static / quasi-static remodeling is feasible now, dynamic-under-crawl waits on the drag fix (engine roadmap T6 cylindrical Stokes drag).
items.principle_note: Replaces the lumped target_z subsample with a mechanistic enzyme process (full-fidelity-over-lumped rule); enzyme kinetics literature-anchored; <z>(c) and c^2 emerge rather than being set. Native scale + full ECM, viewer-verified.

top_autonomous_pick.title: Full macroscopic virial Cauchy stress tensor + method-independent modulus readout for the ECM REV
top_autonomous_pick.why: It is the single unblocking prerequisite for the entire physics-fidelity program: the c-scaling regime characterization, the differential-modulus master curve, negative normal stress, and r^-n stress propagation ALL need one trustworthy, grid-invariant stress — and the library today reads the modulus two inconsistent, boundary-biased ways. It is genuinely autonomous (a measurement/method change, zero parameter tuning), low-risk because it reuses already-validated virial code (_bond_virial_sigma_xz, _bending_virial_sigma_xz, and ff_virial_stress._accum_bond_virial's 1/2 r(x)f construction), and immediately verifiable against the known-modulus PA continuum (E=5000) as ground truth.
top_autonomous_pick.first_concrete_step: In ffn_sim/ff/ecm_mechanics.py, generalize _bond_virial_sigma_xz and _bending_virial_sigma_xz from the single xz component to the full 3x3 sigma tensor, add ecm_material_stress(ecm, pos) -> sigma[3,3] and shear_modulus_virial() (G = sigma_xz/gamma), then run a convergence study on a collagen REV (G vs n_steps in {2k,4k,8k,16k}, box in {16,24,32} um) confirming the virial G plateaus in the Yang-Kaufman band and matches the energy route on the PA continuum both returning E=5000.

lenses.vision: The validated ECM library was built so a CELL can live in it. This roadmap turns the six literature-anchored static substrates into a LIVING substrate: a native full-compartment FF cell that senses stiffness, reads fiber alignment, follows durotactic gradients, and mechanically remodels the matrix — every behavior EMERGENT from the fine-grained FA-clutch bridge (fa_ecm two-sided clutch + substrate.py E→k_sub Winkler), never a lumped mechanosensing law. The strategy splits cleanly around the one open blocker: everything that does NOT require net translocation (stiffness-sensing spread, traction remodeling, contact guidance) is autonomous NOW by wiring the already-built elastic-substrate primitives into the static resting driver, while everything that DOES require migration (durotaxis, stiffness-dependent speed, 3D invasion) is unblocked THROUGH the principled per-segment cylindrical Stokes drag (engine-roadmap T6) that replaces the destabilizing count-scaling --bulk-drag.

phases.name: NEAR — the living static substrate (autonomous, AROUND the blocker)
phases.goal: Make a native full-compartment cell sense, read, and remodel the validated ECM without any net translocation — so the crawl-drag blocker is irrelevant. Every primitive already exists (substrate.py E→k_sub, fa_ecm two-sided clutch, ff_cell_on_substrate resting driver, nematic-S alignment sampler, ecm_remodel_metrics); the work is wiring them together and reading emergent curves.

items.title: Stiffness-sensing spread + traction ladder (soft vs stiff)
items.rationale: The library's headline promise a cell can act on. substrate.py already derives k_sub=2·E·a/(1−ν²) (flat-punch) and has substrate_anchor_equilibrium_kernel, but ff_cell_on_substrate.py still anchors basal clutches to FIXED rigid points — so the cell cannot yet feel E. Wiring the elastic anchor in makes whole-cell traction E-dependent (Bangasser-Odde) purely from the molecular clutches.
items.deliverable: Extended ff_cell_on_substrate.py that consumes resolve_substrate(E); a sweep over the VALIDATED PA recipe ladder (pa_formulation_E ~0.15/1/5/12/40 kPa) at native --from-resting scale on the A5000, emitting spread area (top-down xy-silhouette), summed clutch traction, and bound fraction vs E as JSON + a figs/ curve; the biphasic-vs-monotonic optimum reported as an EMERGENT finding.
items.principle_note: No tuning-to-outcome: k_sub is the DERIVED Boussinesq flat-punch relation and E from validated PA recipes; the biphasic shape is measured, never fit. Absolute traction carries the surfaced adhesion-patch-radius a (PI datum) — held at a literature value and FLAGGED, but the relative E-sweep/optimum is a-invariant so the finding stands. Native --from-resting full-compartment cell; spread uses the ratified top-down silhouette, never contact area.

items.title: Resting-cell traction remodeling of the validated collagen (S6 → static)
items.rationale: S6 already showed a CRAWLING native cell remodels collagen-I (+265 nm) via fa_ecm.py's two-sided clutch. Re-basing onto the STATIC resting cell removes the crawl solver from the loop and lets remodeling be studied as a clean function of the validated collagen state (G'(c), ⟨z⟩, alignment) — the matrix side we can already trust.
items.deliverable: A ff_cell_remodel_static driver: basal FA clutches attach (attach_clutches_to_ecm) to a collagen-I Mikado slab; native-scale run reporting ecm_remodel_metrics (coherent recruit / footprint-radial densification / RAI) vs collagen G' (12 Pa→stiff) and ⟨z⟩ (KB-1.3 target_z), with the traction-OFF control proving the remodel is traction-driven.
items.principle_note: Mechanistic, not lumped: remodeling is the Newton reaction of the fine-grained clutch spring on live fiber nodes (clutch_ecm_spring_kernel), not a traction-field model. No tuning — collagen microstructure is literature-set and its Pa validated; ecm_remodel_metrics separates coherent remodel from passive settling so nothing is over-claimed. Native full-compartment cell on native-extent collagen.

items.title: Contact-guidance traction anisotropy on aligned collagen
items.rationale: The library validated alignment S→anisotropy E∥/E⊥ (1/3/10/63; dermis→TACS-2→TACS-3→tendon). Contact guidance is the cell READING that anisotropy — a resting cell on aligned matrix should show anisotropic traction/protrusion/remodel BEFORE it ever migrates, testable without translocation.

Native scale; a=const so only the anisotropy RATIO (a-invariant) is claimed. Varying S is a legit R-sweep-style lever.

phases.name: MID — the migrating cell (THROUGH the blocker + coupling depth)
phases.goal: Adopt the principled drag law that unblocks native crawl, then let the already-built durotaxis/stiffness substrates drive actual migration; deepen the matrix response to permanent (plastic) remodeling.

items.title: Principled per-segment cylindrical Stokes drag (engine-roadmap T6) — the through-the-blocker fix
items.rationale: Native-crawl 500× slowdown is Σγ∝Nc (count-scaling drag); --bulk-drag destabilizes the solver, --com-drag is a modal patch. Engine roadmap T6 (Kim p03/p13/p14/p22) gives the physical replacement: geometry-derived per-segment Stokes drag ζ=3πμ·r_c·(3+2r₀/r_c)/5 at physiological μ, optionally anisotropic ζ⊥/ζ∥≈1.64 (p43) — grid-invariant by construction.
items.deliverable: A cylindrical-drag module wired into the crawl integrator; a grid-invariance proof (COM velocity + total drag stable as Nc scales coarse→native, unlike --bulk-drag) and a native --from-resting stability demonstration; --bulk-drag kept as superseded fallback.
items.blocker: Native crawl solver stability under per-node drag (standing OPEN item from project-ff-crawl-mechanism) — the law is derived, but its stiffness interaction with the implicit solver at native scale is the risk to retire.
items.principle_note: Explicitly LEGIT lever #2: adding a MISSING REAL force (Stokes drag) at a DERIVED value (μ physiological, r_c fiber radius) — no fit to crawl speed. Grid-invariance is the acceptance test, honoring no-magic-number + native-scale; if it cannot be made stable at native, surface to PI rather than tune.

items.deliverable: Native cell on build_gradient_ecm across the three regimes; up-gradient COM bias measured with a flat-substrate (zero-gradient) control giving ≈0 drift and a seed-robust ensemble, rendered in the cell-on-ECM viewer as a trajectory over the stiffness field.
items.blocker: Blocked by the cylindrical-drag fix (durotaxis requires net translocation).
items.principle_note: Durotaxis EMERGES from the E-dependent clutch (substrate.py) reading build_gradient_ecm's derived local k_sub — no chemotactic-bias term. Zero-gradient control + cross-seed ensemble guard against single-seed artifacts (the S6/crawl lesson). Native full-compartment; gradient values are validated Pa/µm, not tuned.

items.principle_note: One mechanism, two readouts (static traction + migration speed) sharing the DERIVED k_sub — internal consistency is the acceptance check, not a fit. Native scale; a held const so only the E-dependence shape is claimed.

Upgrades remodeling from reversible to durable, matching Chaudhuri/Kim plasticity.

No tuning; stiffness-invariance of relaxation is a built-in falsifier. Native ECM extent.

items.title: ⟨z⟩(c) LOX crosslink-density growth law → collagen c² scaling
items.rationale: The CSCALING_REGIME_FINDING open item: reference-conc Pa is correct but G'(c) exponent is ~1 (density-linear) vs literature ~2 because ⟨z⟩ is held fixed. c² needs ⟨z⟩ to GROW modestly with c while staying above rigidity percolation — a literature-anchored LOX-biology law, explicitly flagged PI-decided.
items.deliverable: A PI-ratified, literature-anchored ⟨z⟩(c) law in build_fibrillar_ecm target_z; re-measured G'(c) exponent for collagen and fibrin; plus fixing the reshape (inextensible) mode's affine-energy divergence so the bending-dominated regime is numerically stable.

Surface the law to PI with its reference before implementing; validate the emergent exponent, don't target it.

items.rationale: Engine-roadmap §3 cross-engine coupling: stiff ECM should feed back to RAISE cortical tension / actin recruitment (mechano-reciprocity), closing the loop so the cortex responds to the substrate it is remodeling — the physiological reality the static experiments approximate as one-way.

Native full-compartment; the one-way (no-feedback) control isolates the reciprocity effect.

top_autonomous_pick.title: Stiffness-sensing spread + traction ladder (soft vs stiff) on the native resting cell
top_autonomous_pick.why: It is the library's core purpose (a cell acting on the ECM), it is fully autonomous and NOT drag-blocked because it requires no translocation, and every primitive already exists — the only gap is that ff_cell_on_substrate.py still anchors basal FA clutches to FIXED rigid points while substrate.py already derives the elastic Winkler anchor k_sub=2·E·a/(1−ν²) and ships substrate_anchor_equilibrium_kernel. Wiring those together immediately yields emergent Bangasser-Odde stiffness sensing across the ALREADY-VALIDATED PA modulus ladder, at native full-compartment scale, with zero tuning (k_sub and E are both derived/validated). It also de-risks the whole mid phase: the same E→k_sub clutch later drives durotaxis and stiffness-dependent motility, so its static optimum becomes the consistency check for those.

Then loop E over the validated PA recipe ladder (pa_formulation_E ~0.15/1/5/12/40 kPa) on the A5000, recording top-down xy-silhouette spread area, summed clutch traction, and bound fraction per E, and plot traction/spread vs E to expose the emergent (not tuned) biphasic optimum — flagging that absolute magnitude carries the surfaced adhesion-patch-radius a while the relative optimum is a-invariant.

items.title: Long-range stress propagation |sigma|(r)~r^-n via a contractile inclusion (KB-1.10)
items.rationale: Verified absent: no stress_propagation/radial-shell code exists, and the only virial in ecm_mechanics.py is the SHEAR sigma_xz component — a radial scalar-invariant stress is genuinely new. This is the single most thesis-defining ECM result: fiber networks transmit stress far beyond the linear-continuum 1/r^3 (Eshelby) prediction, and it doubles as the quasi-static cell-on-ECM bridge (a contracting core IS a model cell).
items.deliverable: New stress_propagation() in ecm_mechanics.py: central spherical Dirichlet core -> inward radial displacement -> relax surrounding net with existing _relax/fixed-mask kernels -> NEW radial scalar-invariant virial (sigma_rr or von Mises per shell, built by extending the sigma_xz virial to the full per-bond+bending tensor, NOT the existing shear-only component) binned into radial shells -> power-law fit n ONLY on a mid-range that spans >=~0.8 decade in r after a box-size convergence check. ff_ecm_stress_propagation.py runs (a) an IN-CODE PA continuum control that MUST recover ~1/r^3 with a SMALL core (r_core << box, e.g. 2um core in a >=10R box) and a far/absorbing or far-pinned boundary, THEN (b) native fibrillar collagen iso vs aligned. JSON + log-log figure with the analytic 1/r^3 overlaid + the fitted mid-range window annotated; interactive HTML stress-field viewer.
items.principle_note: Exponent n EMERGES from the Mikado microstructure — nothing is adjusted to hit any n; growing the box for dynamic range is the legitimate 'more resolution' lever, not fitting. NON-BLOCKING RISK the original plan underweighted: a 5R box with a core of radius R gives r/core~1-2.5 (<half a decade) and pinned-face image stresses corrupt the far field — so the box must be sized (>=10R) with a small core and a far boundary so the PA control ACTUALLY returns 1/r^3 before any fibrillar number is trusted; if dynamic range is still insufficient, report 'insufficient range' honestly rather than fit a short window. Primary ground truth is the in-code analytic continuum control; Kim p13 (radial n~1.2) is on-demand cross-check only. Native by construction.

top_autonomous_pick.title: ECMRemodeler TOPOLOGICAL bond-mutation operator + plasticity/strain-memory channel (break loaded crosslinks → re-form at NEW near-contacts), validated by creep-recovery
top_autonomous_pick.why: It is the single foundational move: MMP (break-only), LOX (form+mature-only), and traction realignment (break/form under a traction field) are all specializations of the same stochastic TOPOLOGICAL bond-mutation, so building it first unlocks the whole near phase. It is genuinely NEW work — verified against the code: the existing xl_turnover_kernel only creeps rest lengths in place (viscoelastic Maxwell) and cannot change topology or reorient fibers, so the topological break/re-form is real net-new physics, not a wrapper. It is genuinely unblocked (traction from a fixed FA patch, no crawl loop) and uses only the STABLE finite-EA path (not the diverging affine-energy reshape); it is not PI-gated (additive mechanism); and the ECMNetwork already stores mutable xl_i/xl_j/xl_k/xl_rest with a target_z-capped _crosslink_near_contacts re-former, so the machinery to mutate exists — only the break-and-reform-at-a-new-partner step is new. It directly delivers a named target the library lacks — KB-1.11 plasticity/strain-memory — as an EMERGENT constitutive behavior, with a smoke discriminator (bond IDENTITIES change, ⟨z⟩ conserved) that cleanly separates it from the pre-existing kernel.
top_autonomous_pick.first_concrete_step: Create ffn_sim/ff/ecm_remodel.py with ECMRemodeler.step(ecm, node_force): (1) compute per-crosslink tension from current positions, (2) apply Bell off-rate k_off(F)=k0·exp(F/F_b) over dt to stochastically BREAK loaded crosslinks by REMOVING their entries from xl_i/xl_j/xl_k/xl_rest (a topology change, NOT the in-place rest-length creep the existing kernel does), (3) re-form crosslinks at CURRENT near-contacts by calling _crosslink_near_contacts on the deformed positions, holding ⟨z⟩ at the KB-1.3 set point. Add a --smoke on a 200-fiber collagen box that imposes a shear and asserts crosslink bond IDENTITIES change (the xl pair-set differs) while ⟨z⟩ is conserved — the discriminator vs the existing rest-length-creep kernel. For the Bell rate, first look up a COLLAGEN/matrix physical-crosslink off-rate in the KB (tag_query); do NOT reuse the Ferrer-2008 α-actinin actin datum — if no matrix datum exists, surface the RATE to PI and proceed with the MECHANISM plus the qualitative emergent permanent-set (any nonzero turnover yields residual>0 / incomplete recovery). Then wire scripts/ff_ecm_plasticity.py to run shear-hold-release through ecm_mechanics and measure residual strain at native scale on the A5000, overlaying the p07 creep-recovery band as an OVERLAY, not a fit.
